answer: A vault bond on earned history blocks a dune of fake accounts. Each applicant locks a non-transferable bond in a vault and files a record of verified work. Auditors compare it with a glacier archive; a mismatch freezes the bond, and a fake loses it, with part paid to the auditor. The k-th fake costs 40+0.05k squared units, since each new fake needs a fresh unclaimed history; 1,000 fakes cost 16,731,675 units. A rented-history ring fails because the glacier archive already credits its work to the original owner, exposing duplicates. An honest agent pays once and earns fees.
